body.en:
Objectives:

  • Remove or reduce pathogens and contaminants to meet applicable drinking-water requirements.
  • Improve clarity, colour, taste and odour where necessary.
  • Produce water that remains stable and safe through storage and distribution.

Plant location: compare source access, elevation and gravity flow, flood risk, soil, power, land for expansion, residuals disposal, approach roads, operator access and proximity to users. Protect the site and arrange adequate monitoring and backup power.

Typical treatment sequence: intake and screening → rapid mixing with coagulant → flocculation → sedimentation → filtration → disinfection and contact → clear-water storage. Aeration or specific contaminant removal may be added. Groundwater and highly polluted sources can require different sequences; not every process removes every contaminant.
body.gu:
Objectives:

  • Pathogens અને contaminants દૂર અથવા ઓછા કરી લાગુ drinking-water requirements સંતોષવી.
  • જરૂર પ્રમાણે clarity, colour, taste અને odour સુધારવાં.
  • Storage અને distribution દરમિયાન સ્થિર તથા safe રહે તેવું પાણી તૈયાર કરવું.

Plant location: source access, elevation અને gravity flow, flood risk, soil, power, expansion માટે land, residuals disposal, approach roads, operator access અને users થી અંતર સરખાવો. Site સુરક્ષિત રાખી યોગ્ય monitoring તથા backup power ગોઠવો.

સામાન્ય treatment sequence: intake અને screening → coagulant સાથે rapid mixing → flocculation → sedimentation → filtration → disinfection અને contact → clear-water storage. જરૂર મુજબ aeration અથવા ચોક્કસ contaminant removal ઉમેરાય છે. Groundwater અને અત્યંત polluted sources માટે અલગ sequence જરૂરી હોઈ શકે; દરેક process બધા contaminants દૂર કરતી નથી.

body.en:
Coagulation: a coagulant such as alum destabilises fine colloids; rapid mixing disperses the chemical. Flocculation: gentle, controlled mixing promotes collisions and forms larger settleable flocs. Dosage depends on raw water, pH and alkalinity; a jar test helps select a dose and operating conditions, and must be confirmed in plant operation.

Sedimentation: water slows in a basin and settleable solids fall by gravity; sludge is collected for safe treatment and disposal. Detention time is theoretical volume divided by flow. Surface overflow rate, inlet/outlet distribution, short-circuiting, floc characteristics and sludge removal also affect performance; detention time alone does not prove performance.
body.gu:
Coagulation: alum જેવા coagulant થી સૂક્ષ્મ colloids ની stability ઘટે છે; rapid mixing chemical ને ફેલાવે છે. Flocculation: ધીમા નિયંત્રિત mixing થી particles અથડાઈ મોટા settleable flocs બને છે. Dosage raw water, pH અને alkalinity પર આધારિત છે; jar test dose અને operating conditions પસંદ કરવામાં મદદ કરે છે, પછી plant operation માં પુષ્ટિ કરો.

Sedimentation: basin માં પાણી ધીમું થતાં settleable solids gravity થી નીચે બેસે છે; sludge ને સલામત treatment અને disposal માટે એકત્ર કરો. Detention time એ theoretical volume ભાગ્યા flow છે. Surface overflow rate, inlet/outlet distribution, short-circuiting, floc characteristics અને sludge removal પણ performance ને અસર કરે છે; ફક્ત detention time થી performance સાબિત થતી નથી.

body.en:
Filter types and working:

  • Slow sand filter: water passes slowly through sand; a biologically active surface layer assists removal. Cleaning typically removes a thin surface layer, with subsequent ripening.
  • Rapid gravity filter: coagulated and settled water passes through media at a higher rate; accumulated solids are periodically removed by controlled backwashing. Underdrains collect filtered water and distribute backwash.
  • Both need monitoring of turbidity, head loss, operating conditions and filter integrity; filtration does not replace disinfection.

Disinfection: chlorine, ozone or ultraviolet light can inactivate pathogens under appropriate conditions. Chlorination provides a residual in distribution, whereas UV has no persistent residual. Chlorine demand is applied dose minus measured residual after a stated contact time. Effectiveness depends on pH, temperature, contact time, disinfectant residual, turbidity and organism; follow the applicable regulatory requirements. Handle chlorine only under trained, approved safety procedures.
body.gu:
Filter ના પ્રકારો અને working:

  • Slow sand filter: પાણી ધીમે sand માંથી પસાર થાય છે; biologically active surface layer removal માં મદદ કરે છે. Cleaning દરમિયાન સામાન્ય રીતે પાતળો surface layer દૂર થાય છે અને પછી ripening થાય છે.
  • Rapid gravity filter: coagulated અને settled water વધુ rate થી media માંથી પસાર થાય છે; જમા solids નિયંત્રિત backwashing થી સમયાંતરે દૂર થાય છે. Underdrains filtered water એકત્ર કરે અને backwash વહેંચે છે.
  • બંનેમાં turbidity, head loss, operating conditions અને filter integrity monitoring જરૂરી છે; filtration disinfection નો વિકલ્પ નથી.

Disinfection: યોગ્ય conditions માં chlorine, ozone અથવા ultraviolet light pathogens ને નિષ્ક્રિય કરે છે. Chlorination distribution માં residual આપે છે, જ્યારે UV persistent residual આપતું નથી. Chlorine demand = લાગુ dose માંથી નિર્દિષ્ટ contact time પછી માપેલ residual બાદ. Effectiveness pH, temperature, contact time, disinfectant residual, turbidity અને organism પર આધારિત છે; લાગુ regulatory requirements અનુસરો. Chlorine માત્ર trained અને approved safety procedures હેઠળ હેન્ડલ કરો.

body.en:
Methods and applications:

  • Softening: lime-soda precipitation or ion exchange reduces calcium and magnesium hardness. Ion-exchange regeneration produces waste brine requiring management.
  • Iron and manganese: aeration or other oxidation followed by appropriate filtration can remove oxidisable forms; pH, oxidation kinetics and source chemistry affect selection.
  • Taste, odour and colour: protect the source and select oxidation, adsorption with activated carbon, coagulation or other treatment according to the cause; avoid assuming one method works for all.
  • Defluoridation: adsorption, the Nalgonda process or membrane treatment can reduce fluoride when correctly designed and operated; monitor treated water and safely manage residuals.
  • Reverse osmosis: pressure-driven membranes reduce many dissolved salts and specific contaminants; pretreatment, membrane maintenance, recovery, concentrate disposal and post-treatment are essential. RO does not by itself guarantee safe distribution.

Confirm effectiveness by testing. Treatment choices and waste handling depend on raw-water composition, scale and local environmental rules.
body.gu:
Methods અને applications:

  • Softening: lime-soda precipitation અથવા ion exchange થી calcium અને magnesium hardness ઘટે છે. Ion-exchange regeneration થી waste brine બને છે જેનું management જરૂરી છે.
  • Iron અને manganese: aeration અથવા અન્ય oxidation પછી યોગ્ય filtration વડે oxidisable forms દૂર થઈ શકે; pH, oxidation kinetics અને source chemistry પ્રમાણે પસંદગી કરો.
  • Taste, odour અને colour: source નું રક્ષણ કરી કારણ મુજબ oxidation, activated carbon adsorption, coagulation અથવા અન્ય treatment પસંદ કરો; એક જ method બધે કામ કરે એમ ન માનો.
  • Defluoridation: યોગ્ય design અને operation હેઠળ adsorption, Nalgonda process અથવા membrane treatment fluoride ઘટાડી શકે; treated water monitor કરો અને residuals નું સલામત management કરો.
  • Reverse osmosis: pressure-driven membranes ઘણા dissolved salts અને ચોક્કસ contaminants ઘટાડે છે; pretreatment, membrane maintenance, recovery, concentrate disposal અને post-treatment જરૂરી છે. ફક્ત RO થી safe distribution ની ખાતરી થતી નથી.

Testing દ્વારા effectiveness ની પુષ્ટિ કરો. Treatment અને waste handling ની પસંદગી raw-water composition, scale અને local environmental rules પર આધારિત છે.

title.gu: Numerical 3.1 — Sedimentation tank નો detention time

body.en:
Given: A tank has effective water volume 900 m³ and steady flow 600 m³/h. Calculate theoretical detention time.

Step 1. Divide effective volume by flow.

t = V / Qt = 900 / 600t = 1.5 h

Step 2. Convert hours to minutes.

t = 1.5 × 60

Final answer:

Theoretical detention time = 90 minutes; actual hydraulic performance also depends on flow pattern.
body.gu:
આપેલ છે: Tank નું effective water volume 900 m³ અને steady flow 600 m³/h છે. Theoretical detention time ગણો.

Step 1. Effective volume ને flow થી ભાગો.

t = V / Qt = 900 / 600t = 1.5 h

Step 2. Hours ને minutes માં ફેરવો.

t = 1.5 × 60

અંતિમ જવાબ:

Theoretical detention time = 90 minutes; actual hydraulic performance flow pattern પર પણ આધારિત છે.

title.en: Numerical 3.2 — Coagulant dose and daily mass
title.gu: Numerical 3.2 — Coagulant dose અને daily mass

body.en:
Given: An operating trial selects alum dose 25 mg/L for a plant treating 4 MLD. Find daily alum mass, assuming 100% active product as specified.

Step 1. Convert flow to litres per day.

Q = 4 × 10⁶ L/day

Step 2. Calculate mass from dose and flow.

Mass = 25 × 4 × 10⁶Mass = 100 × 10⁶ mg/dayMass = 100 × 10⁶ / 10⁶ kg/day

Final answer:

Alum requirement = 100 kg/day for the stated dose and product basis.
body.gu:
આપેલ છે: Operating trial માં 4 MLD plant માટે alum dose 25 mg/L પસંદ થયું છે. નિર્દિષ્ટ મુજબ 100% active product ધારી દૈનિક alum mass શોધો.

Step 1. Flow ને litres per day માં ફેરવો.

Q = 4 × 10⁶ L/day

Step 2. Dose અને flow થી mass ગણો.

Mass = 25 × 4 × 10⁶Mass = 100 × 10⁶ mg/dayMass = 100 × 10⁶ / 10⁶ kg/day

અંતિમ જવાબ:

આપેલ dose અને product basis માટે alum requirement = 100 kg/day.

body.en:
Given: A sample receives a chlorine dose of 2.0 mg/L. Residual after the specified contact time is 0.4 mg/L. Find chlorine demand.

Step 1. Subtract residual from applied dose.

Chlorine demand = applied dose − residualChlorine demand = 2.0 − 0.4

Final answer:

Chlorine demand = 1.6 mg/L for the stated test conditions.
body.gu:
આપેલ છે: Sample ને chlorine dose 2.0 mg/L આપવામાં આવે છે. નિર્દિષ્ટ contact time પછી residual 0.4 mg/L છે. Chlorine demand શોધો.

Step 1. Applied dose માંથી residual બાદ કરો.

Chlorine demand = applied dose − residualChlorine demand = 2.0 − 0.4

અંતિમ જવાબ:

આપેલ test conditions માટે chlorine demand = 1.6 mg/L.
